◎

The 192–252-bit screen has a real split. Of 537 exact models, 247 pass the necessary cubic-depth test but still need a cover witness; 137 fail that depth test, and 153 fall outside the recorded genus-three domain. Their selected-subgroup advantages remain unmeasured. Open a row to inspect both branch screens.

◇

Oakley Groups 3 and 4 have separate GHS finding IDs. Their field degrees split as 5 × 31 and 5 × 37. The exact GHS magic number is five for the recorded route, while the genus-15 cover and attack cost are formula projections. Their full group orders have cofactors 12 and 4 around large prime factors; the subgroup and implementation questions are distinct. Read the WID1 specification ↗

∴

Pairing groups and protocol attacks have distinct goals. Ethereum BN_SNARK1 and BLS12-381 now expose G1, G2, GT, subgroup parameters and the minimal root-of-unity field. Pairing availability is intentional for these curves. The SIKEp434 protocol case records the published auxiliary-torsion key-recovery attack separately from ordinary isogeny maps.

A shared trace proves existence of an isogeny over the finite field; it does not give an explicit map. A certified map is a route ingredient, while a weakness assessment also needs selected-subgroup transport and a cheaper destination method. The graph contains a bounded, verified walk, not every isogeny in these classes.

03 / Recognize

— criteria, distinct gates

Filter by the stated security goal and check stage. DDH requires a decision witness, static DH requires a reused-key oracle, subgroup misuse requires an implementation, and SIDH depends on auxiliary torsion images. GLV and GLS remain arithmetic screens.

04 / Coverage

The extension-field map

Prime extension degree, a hyperelliptic equation, and an efficient discrete-log route are separate facts. The current atlas records published families and names the missing exact-model checks.

01 / PRIME-DEGREE COVER

36 parameter cases

The odd-characteristic classification covers relative degrees 2, 3, 5, and 7. Its cases still need exact equations, genus, and subgroup maps for individual atlas models.

02 / DIRECT DECOMPOSITION

Work on E itself

Extension-field index calculus uses a subfield factor base and summation-polynomial decompositions. It needs measured natural relation yield and target recovery; no cover is required.

03 / JACOBIAN ISOGENY

A cubic route without a cover

A published construction maps some prime-order cubic-extension groups to genus-three Jacobians through a Weil-restriction isogeny. Exact isogeny and kernel checks are open here.

04 / HYPERELLIPTIC GEOMETRY

Same-field covers are common

Verified degree-two or degree-three covers exist for supported models over their original fields. A smaller-field destination and a costed subgroup transfer are separate requirements.

The genus-three destination may also be nonhyperelliptic, so each record must state its curve model and arithmetic backend. The source-linked coverage audit ↗ tracks the open construction and measurement gates.

05 / Verify

From a lead to a measured route

ICV1 identifies the exact curve model. WID1 identifies one criterion on that model and selected scope; its grade can improve while its ID stays fixed.

01 / Identity

Fix the model

Record field representation, equation, trace, point count, and a stable model identity. A class result does not identify every model in that class.

02 / Criterion

Check the hypothesis

Compute the trace, factor the selected order, calculate embedding degree, or realize a covering. Preserve exceptional cases and negative results.

03 / Transfer

Certify the map

For pairings and coverings, exhibit a nondegenerate or injective map for the chosen subgroup and target. Record any kernel intersection.

04 / Cost

Measure the work

Include construction and transport costs, then compare a verified target under a matched resource contract.

Exact criterion a checked model and the stated mathematical condition Geometry a positive cover-model signal Candidate an unresolved transfer or cost gate

06 / Provenance

Trace each row back

The snapshot is deterministically exported from two source-locked SQLite databases and the repository's named-curve and transfer registries. The Oakley parameters are checked against their RFCs; Sage independently checks their points and prime-order subgroup generators.
